about: Exient's software renderer (SSX Out of Bounds): triangles sorted far to near, each drawn by one of two functions through a span filler picked by the material: 8-bit textures with a palette per light level, colour ramps, flat colours, half-transparent and keyed variants.

hooks.note: The 3D of a frame starts: the sorted list of triangles is emptied. r0 is the renderer. The target is the screen buffer from its first row to the last row of the view (176 by 176, 16 rows down in a race).

A triangle: r0 the renderer, r1 three vertices of 12 bytes (x, y in quarter pixels of the view, u, v in 128ths of a texel, shade, depth), r2 the material (+0x18 texture or colour, +0x1c palette, +0x20 mode).

vars.pal: u32(r2 + 0x1c) + sel($rows, min(31, max(0, sar($shade, 5))), sel($m & 0x80, 0, sar($L, 5))) * 512

hooks.note: Clipping at the top of the view: where each corner of the triangle moves to.
Textured, opaque: 64 by 64 texels of 8 bits, 256 bytes a row, through one of 64 palettes picked by the light (or the one palette, mode bit 0x80). Bit 0x40 corrects perspective per pixel.
Textured, index 0 transparent (bit 2).
Textured, half and half with the picture (bit 4), or every other pixel (bit 0x20).
Textured, every other pixel, index 0 transparent.
Untextured, shaded: each pixel takes the colour ramp entry (32 entries of 12 bits) of the shade interpolated across the triangle, dithered; the ramp is drawn as a texture.
Untextured, shaded, every other pixel (bit 0x20): drawn as half and half.
Untextured, one colour: the material's 12-bit colour through the light.
Untextured, one colour, half and half (bit 4) or every other pixel (bit 0x20).
A quad: the same arguments, with four vertices.

vars.pal: u32(r2 + 0x1c) + sel($rows, min(31, max(0, sar($shade, 5))), sel($m & 0x80, 0, sar($L, 5))) * 512

hooks.note: Clipping at the top of the view: where each corner of the triangle moves to.
The same for the quad's second triangle (vertices 0, 2, 3).
